mappings.note: The root of the quarrel, which the key states as compassion against self-interest -- reading the idea beneath the plot. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: no line names that opposition.
The moral lesson the whole story is told to deliver -- the text's usefulness. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2, which is detail-finding.
Explication of 'rakshak par bhakshak ko vaare' -- unpacking the poet's stated idea. Rejected C-HIN4.1-LO-1: the difficulty is the proposition, not the words.
Rahul's view of justice, to be set out and explained. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: a position, not a locatable fact.

Asks what WE should do when an innocent creature is killed -- the learner's own reasoned response to cruelty to animals, a natural-world issue. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the stance called for is the learner's, not an appraisal of the poet's.

Requires showing how the poem turns from garden beauty to pathos -- following the poet's construction. Rejected C-HIN1.1-LO-3, which is oral rendering of a scene one has seen, not analysis of a poem's turn.
Argue in writing why one line is the poem's most important -- a defended preference. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the task is to justify a choice, not to agree or disagree with the poet.
Poet plus an introduction to the source composition -- placing and appraising the whole work. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: nothing inside the extract answers it.
Character study of the hunter, which the key extends to what he symbolises. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: the traits are inferred across the poem, not found in a line.
Explication of the 'nyaay daya ka daani' claim. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: this is one proposition, not the text's overall use.
How the poem portrays a child's mind -- reading the poet's method. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: not about usefulness but about technique of characterisation.
How the poem establishes the worth of compassion -- its governing purpose. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: no single detail carries it.

'Do YOU think the hunter was right' -- invites the learner's own reasoned position on killing a mute creature for sport. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the object of judgement is the practice, not the poet's idea.
Speaker attribution for a refrain line inside the printed extract -- close examination for a specific point. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: no interpretation needed.
What fell from above, answered from the extract. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: bare detail.
Who lifted the swan, from the extract. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the act's meaning is asked elsewhere.
Where the flowers bloomed -- setting detail located in the extract. Rejected C-HIN1.1-LO-3: no scene has to be rendered, only named.
Condition and direction of the swan's fall -- two details from the verse. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: no gist required.
Whom Yashodhara asks to judge -- specific point in the extract. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the verdict's reasoning is a separate item.
Who is listening to the story, from the extract. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: bare detail.
Who speaks the line 'nyaay daya ka daani' -- attribution. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: its meaning is asked in a different item.
What Yashodhara says to Rahul -- restating the located speech. Rejected C-HIN4.2-LO-2, which covers writing others' words in one's own way as a composition task.
The decision Rahul reaches, as the extract states it. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the item asks what, not why.
Who asked for the wounded bird. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: detail, not usefulness.
Who protected the wounded bird. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: no appraisal of the protection.
Who resolved to be obstinate. Rejected C-HIN4.1-LO-1: 'hath' is not the tested item, the agent is.
Who saved the bird, short answer from the extract. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: bare detail.
Why the father refused the hunter -- the extract supplies the reason. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: no independent judgement asked.
Who speaks the poem's opening line -- attribution. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-1: detail.
What the boy insists on being told. Rejected C-HIN3.1-LO-1: the story he wants is a literary tale, not folk material he is to appreciate.
Who speaks 'tu hai hathi, maandhan mere' -- attribution. Rejected C-HIN4.1-LO-1: the diction of that line is tested in the next item, not here.
Title and poet of the extract -- bibliographic placement. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: not found inside the verse.
The argument Rahul offers to get a story -- located in the extract. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-2: the learner reports his argument rather than making one.
Whom the words 'hathi' and 'maandhan' refer to -- attending to the fine grain of the poet's diction. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: the demand is lexical, not narrative.
Meaning of 'taat' -- a new word from this text. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: no detail is being located.

Identifies the natural image (dewdrops) carried by a poetic line -- appreciation of poetic imagery. Cited at goal level because none of the 16 outcomes covers kaavya-bimb: C-HIN3.1-LO-1 is folk songs and tales specifically, and C-HIN4.1-LO-1 covers the learner's own use of words, not a poet's imagery.
The boy's reaction, evidenced by the refrain he keeps repeating -- a point located by close reading. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: the evidence is explicit in the extract.
Glosses the phrase 'surabhi manmaani' word by word -- fine grain of vocabulary and phrase. Rejected CG-HIN3: the key treats it as a lexical gloss, not as appreciation of the image.
What the mother asked Rahul to do -- specific point in the extract. Rejected C-HIN2.1-LO-1: no reasoning required.
Meaning of 'tune guni kahaani' -- the archaic verb 'gunna' is the whole difficulty. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: lexical, not narrative.
Meaning of 'nirapraadh' -- vocabulary. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2 on the same ground.
What Rahul ties justice to -- grasping the conceptual link the poet makes between justice and mercy. Rejected C-HIN4.1-LO-1: the two words are easy; the link is the point.
Which qualities of Rahul the extract reveals -- inference across the passage. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: no line lists them.
Meaning of 'aakhetak' -- vocabulary. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: the word, not the character, is tested.
Who lifted the swan, keyed to 'taat' in this extract. Rejected C-HIN4.1-LO-1: 'taat' is glossed in its own item.
Meaning of the compound 'lakshya-siddhi'. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: lexical demand.
What the father must have FELT -- the conditional invites the learner to supply an unstated inner response. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: nothing in the extract states it.
The difference between hunter and father, which the key frames as protector against predator -- reading the poem's contrast. Rejected C-HIN2.2-LO-2: the contrast is drawn, not found.
